MIND. [1] [Æth.]
Unable to read after overexertion of mental faculties.
Incapacity to think ; confused.
Idiocy, in some cases alternating with furor.
Hallucinations.
Imagined she saw rats run across room.
Delirium : imagines he sees cats and dogs ; jumps out of window ; even with the chill.
Well-disposed, serene, in forenoon ; in afternoon, ill-humored, anxious and sad.
Great sadness when alone.
Great anxiety and restlessness ; soon afterwards, violent pains in head and abdomen.
Bad humor, irritability, especially in afternoon, and in open air.
Anxiety and restlessness. θ Megrim.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Æth.]
Head confused ; brain feels bound up.
Vertigo : with sleepiness, can't raise head ; giddiness ceases and head gets hot ; with palpitation.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Æth.]
Sensation as if both sides of head were in a vise.
Pressing pain in forehead, as if it would split ; at its height vomiting and finally diarrhœa.
All day throbbing pain in left forehead, temple and side of head, > by pressure (felt as though she would like a band tightly fixed around head) and in open air, < by walking.
Headache with vertigo, < walking and looking upward.
Headache since five weeks, after checked menses.
   

OUTER HEAD. [4] [Æth.]
Distressing pain in occiput, nape and down spine, > by friction with hot whiskey.
Inability to hold head erect or to sit up.
Sensation as if she was constantly pulled by the hair.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Æth.]
Pupils dilated, but sensitive to touch.
Pupils dilated, staring eyes, stupid. θ Cholera infantum.
Eyes brilliant and protruding.
Eyeballs turned downward. θ Convulsions of children.
Pustules on cornea.
Chronic inflammation of edges of eyelids.
Adhesion of eyelids in morning, requiring them to be softened by a fluid to prevent pulling out lashes.
Scrofulous ophthalmia ; swelling of Meibomian glands.
   

SMELL AND NOSE. [7] [Æth.]
Herpetic eruption at end of nose.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Æth.]
Face pale. θ Megrim.
Face sunken, earthy pale, withered. θ Cholerine.
Heat in face with trembling in head. θ Cholerine.
A drawn condition, beginning at alæ nasi, and extending to angle of mouth, gave face an expression of great anxiety and pain.
The features have an expression of anguish and pain.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Æth.]
Feeling as if tongue was too long. θ Aphthæ.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Æth.]
Intolerance of milk.
   

EATING AND DRINKING. [15] [Æth.]
Regurgitation of food an hour or so after eating.
Suitable to children who cannot bear milk.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Æth.]
Spasmodic hiccough. θ Megrim. θ Cholerine.
Empty eructation. θ Megrim.
Violent sudden vomiting ; of a frothy milk-white substance ; of yellow fluid, followed by curdled milk and cheesy matter.
Vomiting of greenish phlegm, similar to stools.
The milk is forcibly ejected soon after taken ; then weakness causes drowsiness. θ Nursing children.
Profuse vomiting of water. θ Young children.
Copious greenish vomiting.
Gripes accompanied by fearful vomiting, weakness and indescribable anguish.
Vomiting spells at height of headache. θ Megrim.
After vomiting, cold and clammy. θ Cholera infantum.
   

SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Æth.]
Pain in pit of stomach and abdomen, followed by nausea, with or without vomiting.
Cramp in stomach. θ Megrim.
Painful contractions of stomach so severe as to prevent vomiting. θ Cholerine.
   

HYPOCHONDRIA. [18] [Æth.]
Painfulness of epigastric region, nausea.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Æth.]
Colic, with diarrhœa.
Excessive griping pain in abdomen.
Colic, followed by vomiting, vertigo and weakness.
Cutting and violent vomiting.
Cutting, with distension of abdomen.
Abdomen puffed sensitive to touch ; convulsions of children. θ Gastroenteritis.
Sensation of coldness in abdomen.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Æth.]
A thin stool finishes headache. θ Megrim.
Stools of partly digested food, shortly after a meal or at night.
Diarrhœa ; discharges green, thin, bilious, with violent tenesmus before and after stool. θ Convulsions of children. θ Gastroenteritis.
Bright yellow or greenish, watery, slimy stools ; crying, drawing up feet. Child, æt. 6 months.
Greyish-green fluid stools. θ Cholerine.
With stools, painful contraction in stomach. θ Cholerine.
Most obstinate constipation, with feeling as if all action of bowels had been lost.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Æth.]
Urine : red, sediment white ; copious, clear as water ; too frequent after exertion.
No urine. θ Cholerine.
   

FEMALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [23] [Æth.]
Menses checked by a warm bath. θ Headache.
   

PREGNANCY. PARTURITION. LACTATION. [24] [Æth.]
Intolerance of milk ; child by a sudden and violent effort throws it up, curdled or not ; then weakness makes it drowsy for some minutes.
   

VOICE AND LARYNX. TRACHEA AND BRONCHIA. [25] [Æth.]
No voice. θ Cholerine.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Æth.]
Palpitation : with headache ; with vertigo ; with weariness and exaltation ; t.
Pulse frequent, small, some what hard and unrhythmical.
Weak intermittent pulse, with palpitation and headache.
Pulse feeble, sometimes not to be felt, much exhausted. θ Cholerine.
   

UPPER LIMBS. [32] [Æth.]
Thumb and fingers bent inward. θ Convulsions of children.
   

LOWER LIMBS. [33] [Æth.]
Excoriations of thighs from walking.
   

NERVES. [36] [Æth.]
Trembling at heart with anxious restlessness.
Epileptic spasms, with clenched thumbs, red face, eyes turned downward, pupils fixed, dilated ; foam at mouth, jaws locked ; small, hard and quick pulse.
Spasms, with stupor and delirium.
General malaise.
Convulsions. θ Gastroenteritis.
Weakness after colic.
Great weakness ; children cannot stand ; cannot hold up head.
Great weakness and prostration, with sleepiness.
He lies stretched out without consciousness.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Æth.]
Dozing of child after vomiting spells or after stool.
On falling asleep, rolling of eyes or slight convulsions.
Sleep after headache. θ Megrim.
   

ATTACKS, PERIODICITY. [41] [Æth.]
Periodical headache. θ Megrim.
   

SKIN. [46] [Æth.]
Cool skin. θ Cholerine.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Æth.]
Children, during dentition.
Old woman during cholera season. θ Cholerine.
